title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 93
paragraphs: Socles, the envoy of Corinth, spoke thus; and Hippias made answer to him, calling to witness the same gods as Socles had, that assuredly the Corinthians, more than any others, would one day regret the loss of the sons of Peisistratus, when the appointed days came for them to be troubled by the Athenians. Thus Hippias made answer, being better acquainted with the oracles than any other man. But the rest of the allies, who for a time had restrained themselves and kept silence, when they heard Socles speak freely, all gave voice to what they felt, and adopted the opinion of the Corinthian envoy, adjuring the Lacedaemonians not to do any violence to a Hellenic city.
